item.title: Taiwan and the UK sign space industry pact to deepen supply chain cooperation
item.description: Six months after Taiwan and the United Kingdom held their first Taiwan–UK Space Industry Roundtable in Taiwan in September 2025, the two sides have taken another step toward deeper cooperation in the space sector.

item.title: Phison rides AI wave to record profits; foresees explosive growth through 2026
item.description: Phison Electronics Corp. (TPEX: 8299), a global leader in NAND flash controllers and storage solutions, has reported a blockbuster fourth quarter for 2025, driven by an insatiable global appetite for AI-ready storage. The company posted record-breaking revenue of $719 million (NT$22.8 billion), with EPS hitting an all-time high of NT$21.74.

item.title: Defense chips, satellite systems now "100% localized," Chinese academics say
item.description: As conflict in the Middle East intensifies and geopolitical risks rise, governments worldwide are paying closer attention to the resilience of defense supply chains and semiconductor self-sufficiency. Against this backdrop, and as China convenes its annual "Two Sessions," an article jointly authored by several Chinese academicians and published in the state-backed journal Science & Technology Review has drawn attention.

item.title: Broadcom CEO sees copper interconnects viable through 2028
item.description: Broadcom reported strong results for the first quarter of fiscal 2026, driven by robust demand for cloud application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), and issued an upbeat outlook. During the earnings call, however, industry attention centered less on the company's financial performance and more on its views on silicon photonics and copper interconnect technologies.

item.title: SpaceX shifts from GaAs as scalable silicon and perovskite solar technologies advance
item.description: In early 2026, Tesla CEO Elon Musk visited China to inspect its solar supply chain, focusing on back-contact, heterojunction, and perovskite technologies. This move suggests a reevaluation of SpaceX's future space solar power plans, highlighting a shift from prioritizing performance to emphasizing cost efficiency and scalability.

item.title: Tier-1 orders from major automakers fueling growth for Hiroca
item.description: The Chinese automotive market is undergoing an unprecedented transformation amid increasing industry volatility. As new energy vehicle (NEV) penetration rapidly rises, the traditional internal combustion engine (ICE) segment continues to shrink. Coupled with ongoing price wars, automakers face fierce competition on retail pricing while imposing stricter cost controls and faster R&D demands on their supply chains.

item.title: DynaPack plans triple BBU capacity expansion to meet AI data center demand
item.description: With AI data centers now integrating battery backup units (BBU), battery module maker DynaPack plans to add an additional 200% to its production capacity at its Taiwan and Thailand facilities to capitalize on this clearly emerging trend, with room for further growth. In addition, the company has several ongoing projects to develop BBUs tailored for high-voltage direct current (HVDC) systems, targeting mass production as early as 2027.

item.title: Applied Materials VP warns AI growth may hit energy, not chip limits
item.description: AI is rapidly driving global computing demand and accelerating semiconductor industry growth. Applied Materials vice president Erix Yu expects the semiconductor market to reach US$1 trillion in revenue in 2026—earlier than previous forecasts.

item.title: Adata chairman expects NAND price surge in 2H26
item.description: Memory module giant Adata reported record-high operations in 2025, with chairman Simon Chen forecasting a strong memory market throughout 2026. He highlighted that upstream manufacturers' inventory levels have dropped to critically low points, supporting their confidence for aggressive price hikes.

item.title: Global auto giants retreat to 'survival defense' as electrical revolution triggers CEO reshuffle
item.description: The global automotive industry is currently navigating its most seismic leadership transition in decades as the Electronic/Electrical (E/E) revolution fundamentally rewrites the rules of competition.
